segmentSplit.title: Government vs Commercial revenue
segmentSplit.content:
Palantir reports two operating segments: Government (US and allied defense/intelligence agencies) and Commercial (enterprise customers, US and international).

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: Commercial was the smaller, slower-growing book for years; since AIP's 2023 launch it has been growing faster than Government on both US and international legs, which is the bull case for a re-rating away from a pure defense-contractor multiple.

What to watch:

  • Commercial share of total revenue rising, not just its absolute growth rate
  • Government growth re-accelerating or staying lumpy around US budget cycles
  • Log scale here so the two segments' growth paths are comparable despite the size gap

adjOperatingMargin.title: Adjusted operating margin
adjOperatingMargin.content:
Adjusted operating margin is Palantir's own non-GAAP measure: operating income before stock-based compensation and certain one-off items, divided by revenue.

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: GAAP operating margin is held down by heavy SBC, so this is the figure management and most sell-side models actually target when they talk about operating leverage; it has expanded sharply as revenue has scaled against a slower-growing cost base.

What to watch:

  • Margin trend versus revenue growth (operating leverage, not just cost cuts)
  • The gap to GAAP operating margin -- it is the SBC add-back, not free money

remainingDealValue.title: Remaining Deal Value (RDV)
remainingDealValue.content:
Remaining Deal Value is the total value of contracted deals not yet recognised as revenue -- Palantir's own forward-bookings metric, split by Government and Commercial.

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: this is the KPI analysts watch for forward demand before it shows up in revenue, especially on the Commercial side where large multi-year AIP deals are booked upfront. Disclosed only in the annual report (FY2023-FY2025 so far) -- there is no quarterly or half-year breakout, so this chart always shows just three points.

What to watch:

  • RDV growth outpacing revenue growth (bookings leading billings)
  • Commercial RDV share rising, confirming the segment-mix shift seen in revenue

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Palantir Technologies Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
